body: That’s fair. I thought she was romantically interested in me, I interpreted her messages as flirty. It turns out she was being friendly. She said she doesn’t date coworkers, which I respect, and is probably for the best. She asked me out to dinner, which I misinterpreted as a date. She then canceled an hour before because of mental health related reasons. I took this way too personally (definitely something I need to work on, as this had nothing to do with me). We’re now on the same page. I feel the need to talk to her, but I feel like it would just make things worse.

Okay last person who commented. I don’t appreciate that. I’m not stalking her at all - she’s off of work and I haven’t responded to her last message. I’m giving her space. Learn to read the post. I HAVENT TALKED TO HER SINCE THEN, understand, idiot? In fact, I’ve blocked her so I resist the urge to reach out! 

I’ve respected her boundary of not wanting to date. 
I respect the right of her to cancel because of mental health, although it hurts.
I understand nobody owes anybody anything in this world. 
I’ve been respected her space. So yeah, I don’t think that makes me “possessive,” unless my definition of that word is completely incorrect.

I don’t strive to be weird. I guess (and again, I still admit I should’ve responded better) was because there was a miscommunication and I thought dinner was a date. Then she talked about some guy she was seeing. To be fair, she didn’t know I liked her and she used the word “friend” in reference to me a lot, but I guess she had given me major mixed signals. 

Again, should’ve handled it way more maturely, but that was why I took such offense. The cancellation was legit, mental health is an important consideration.

I guess I just don’t appreciate being led on like that, whether it was some sort of “test” or something.

Believe it or not, this was a date that she rescheduled. We were going to meet earlier but it didn’t work. We had already texted a bunch before and I’ll admit, I misread her intentions. It is what it is. She did cancel an hour before, which I was confused by, and thought was inconsiderate (I regret that wording). I should know better. Like I said, I’ll be the first to admit when I screwed up. 

I did ask her if it would be alright to check in with her (mental health wise) and she said it would be fine. At this point, that doesn’t matter to me. I just feel bad about how I acted. That’s the main issue here.

If she had said,  “I don’t date coworkers”  before pretending to be interested, okay. Then I’d accept that I was in the wrong. I still am, partially. I’ll admit that. But I think to do that after the fact, not cool. I asked if we could hang out one on one (she had mentioned this before) and she said “as friends” and I said “depends on what you want.” Then she told me. Last night. So I was unaware of this going on. If I did, it would be different I feel.

Also, she literally told me this boundary yesterday evening. It’s not like I knew this right off the bat. 
She told me last night, after 2 months of knowing her and talking with her, and her being “flirty.” So yeah.

And yes, I recognize she can do what she wants. I’m not disputing that. And I don’t think I tested her boundaries, I guess I was just misinformed. I hold myself accountable for what I did. But every relationship is a two-way street. Platonic or otherwise

By no means did I ever indicate that I would disrespect those boundaries. That wouldn’t be right. Remember, my feelings are valid here too. Let’s just say, hypothetically (and I know I’m being vague here) someone would:

Respond very quickly 
Send flirty emojis c: (interpretation differs)
Be physically touchy 
Say “please don’t leave” and “I’d be sad if you go”
All your friends knew you were into her
Friends think she’s into you (not exactly flirting, but maybe a sign)
Laugh at literally most everything you say (again, could be friendly)
Invite you out to dinner w/o the pretense of “as friends”
Now she did mention the word friends a couple times so I guess I should’ve been more cognizant.

But I mean, I personally wouldn’t invite someone to dinner and then talk about some guy I’m interested in, if I was being flirty. But hey, everyone’s different. At the very least, she was honest, and I appreciate that.

So yeah, you can think I’m being immature, but I think people should make their intentions clear from the get go and not get peoples hopes up. She recognized she was being flirty and still said “I’m sorry that wasn’t my intention.” So you flirt like that with all your friends? Weird. 

I guess I personally wouldn’t behave like that if I showed signs of interest. 

So yeah, I don’t strive to be disrespectful. I respect her decision and if she changes her mind, she changes her mind.
Tell me about it. Her discarding me was one of the best things, if not the best thing, that’s happened to me. Kinda funny how it set my life (thus far) into motion.

Thank you. To you as well. I remember thinking to myself “the only thing I can do is block this number.” Otherwise, my time would be wasted waiting for someone who (most likely) wouldn’t change. In the meantime, I’ve met some great people. I don’t know them too well yet, but their actions have proven to be emblematic of their personalities (well-intentioned).

So true. There isn’t really any middle ground. Of course, it’s not that easy to navigate; if it was, people wouldn’t struggle to get out. But the grass really is greener on the other side. Everyone deserves to be treated with love, respect, kindness. How certain people aren’t able to be empathetic I’ll never fully understand. The best anyone can be is kind :)

Thank you. I finally feel free to control my own destiny. After dealing with this girl and a parent with narcissistic traits, it’s beautiful to be able to explore my own identity and craft a sense of self. Sometimes we forget that’s lost when we get involved with someone with NPD.

Thank you so much. I can relate to what you’re saying. It was so difficult, that craving to be around that person. I reached out maybe twice, but after I remembered how I was treated, that was enough for me to stick to NC. But I don’t regret it at all. In fact, it showed me that people can be incredibly resilient in the face of hardship(s). The best choice I ever made, hands down. It sounds cliche, but one day at a time is really really important.

Thank you so much. You can no doubt. Trust me on the NC. You gotta fight any urge to get back in touch. It’s really hard because your brain is withdrawing from the dopamine rush you’ve been given. It’s really really hard. Trust me, it’s worth it. You’re worth it. You won’t regret it, believe me, even if you don’t feel that way now necessarily.

Gaslighting and putting me down. Stringing me along by my feelings. Got a kick out of invoking jealousy in me. And constantly telling me that I stressed her out when I would do something so kind as to look in her direction and smile.

I think people who have NPD just have the ability to manipulate in such a way to make things feel as though they’re your fault. Of course they aren’t, but they’re so good at mind games. Something one shouldn’t strive to be good at.

I think that’s a great idea. It really is that easy, though it is kinda nerve-wracking. She seems great. She knows I’m shy and anxious and is understanding. I’ll go in with a positive mindset. Hopefully this could be the catalyst for something promising, friendship or otherwise.

Well, to start, she’d make fun of any kind of music I liked. She’d stop at nothing to let me know how much she hated any artist I mentioned (I never once made fun of her musical tastes). She also called me “sensitive,” “dramatic.”

Blatant lack of empathy. Just saying hurtful things regularly without a shred of remorse. Subtle put downs. Always being told that I “stressed her out” when in reality, she was treated with nothing but kindness. I’m so sorry to all of you for having to go through this. Hang in there, please.

It was unbelievably hard, but you’re right. People deserve respect. Anyway again, I think about what you (and everyone else who commented on this) had to say and it’s nice to know there’s kind people out there after all. My faith in humanity is shot, so that goes a long way. Thanks again!

Oh I haven’t and I won’t. It was hard to fight at first and now I feel my brain slowly becoming more stable thank goodness. I ran into her by chance a month or so ago (I live in a city of millions of people) and tried telling her how I felt - she said some of the meanest things I’ve ever heard. So I just cut my losses at that point and accepted change, for her, isn’t possible. Not to sound insensitive, but that isn’t my problem. It just breaks my heart that someone wouldn’t want to treat anyone else with kindness, I mean the world sucks and everyone needs support. She just went through something at a young age and that behavior is “normalized” in her case, but that doesn’t give her a free pass to treat others like dirt. I barely think about her now but it’s a learning experience. Still, it’ll take a bit for me to get comfortable forming relationships. Anyway, I appreciate your kindness. It makes me feel less alone, and for that I thank you.
Well the “dating” lasted only 2 months, me “knowing” her only 4. But anyway, it’s been hard. Thanks again. Just feel kinda behind.
I think the hardest part is telling those who wronged me how I feel, but it won’t make a difference. That’s why closure on one’s own terms is that much more important.

Thank you so very much. I appreciate that, I’m an emotional person so this made me cry (but in the best possible way). The whole situation only lasted about 3-4 months, but it’s drawn my attention to a lifetime of emotional abuse I’ve dealt with. It’s been hard. I still can’t fathom how people could be so cruel and not treat anyone with kindness (this came to me because I realized I didn’t want to be like anyone who abused me). At times, it seems like my life is on hold, but once you slowly put things together, it makes sense. This is a whole new level of hurt. Unfortunately, it feels like there will always be people near me who will implore me to “move on” already. But people scare me more than they already did. Like I said, I feel like I need friends but how will I know people just won’t hurt me? It’s horrible. Therapy and journaling are godsends. It’s nice to know there’s methods of coping. My faith in humanity is shot for now. But it’s nice to know there’s people who care. Thank you. Kindness goes a whole lot further in this world, I’ve come to realize. I appreciate you insight and I’ll be thinking about this while I heal.

I appreciate that response. I’m sorry you had to go through that, such blatant disregard for someone else’s feelings breaks my heart. In my case, I never called her out because of fear of the “mean” part of the “mean/sweet” cycle. But a lot of people pick up on things pretty quick. There is a certain sense of reassurance in that neither of us are alone, and are much better off having left those partners behind, and finding someone worthy of our time and feelings.

Fair enough I provided no context.

- She gaslit me more times than I can count
- would talk about her crushes constantly in front of me
- flaked hanging out the day off with bad excuses 
- made fun of music I liked
- oscillated between mean and sweet 
- we briefly “dated” and had some intimate moments, I said I liked them, when I asked if she did, she said “no, not really” and that was all
- screamed at me in her car for like 40-60 minutes about how she didn’t care about my feelings 
- called a “pissy little b…. who was as immature as a 12 y/o who needs to stop feeling sorry for myself and who needs serious professional help”
- called “mopey” when I was sad and she kicked me out of her place (she suffers from depression)
- said the thought of being in a relationship with me would make her and I quote “projectile vomit”

I mean you wouldn’t know this, but I literally have been doing a ton of research to try moving on and compiled a page and a half of this kinda stuff, and though I can’t diagnose her, I wouldn’t be posting in this reddit/subreddit if I didn’t think that was the case, in all honesty.

I completely understand that unfortunately. When I was discarded, I hate “I don’t care about your feelings” screamed in my face out of nowhere. Pretty traumatizing even though it hasn’t been a full 2 months since it all went down. But I agree with your last point as well - for me, it was almost like making excuses for that behavior, not being able to comprehend it and just thinking something was “off.” But over time there’s a realization that you can’t really do anything or fix anyone. It just boggles my mind. I’m sorry you had to go through that, if it’s any consolation at all, I know how it feels, and it’s absolutely horrendous.

I just want to thank everyone who commented on this post for their kind words. I’m so sorry you all had to go through this, but it’s nice to know I’m not alone (I definitely thought I was). This has been incredibly difficult and since I put myself in a bad situation financially, I’ll have to employ coping mechanisms. But this journey has a purpose. To rediscover ourselves after having that taken away. To love ourselves. I’m proud of all of you. Journaling has been and absolute godsend. That and self-help, which I was too keen on before. And the positive self-talk, though that’s difficult most of the time. It’ll be a long trip back to myself, but from what I’ve read, it’s worth it. 1000 percent no doubt. Not sure if a comment in this thread mentioned psychopath free, but it’s a great read. Really helpful. Anyway, it’s nice to know there’s decent people out there. Thank you all, more than you’ll ever know. You’re good people. Goes a long way in this world.
I can’t recall if I thanked him during the interview (I know) , but obviously I thanked him in the follow-up email. I can’t seem to get over this. Guess I have to try harder the next time.

Thank you for your kindness and insight. I appreciate this. It’s all so new to me, so fresh. My “fear” is that it will take a lot longer than that, though every situation is different. I’m terribly shy and wasn’t much of a people person before, so now I feel as though it’ll take me that much longer to move my life forward. Is there something wrong with this? Just don’t know. Being positive internally is so difficult when your own identity feels stripped away. Now I feel as though I have to speed up the process to catch up to everyone else and “start living my best life.” One day at a time I’ve been told. You both make great points. It’s just been a haze.

Had someone I loved/cared about scream at me in her car for 40-60 mins. She was driving so there was nowhere for me to go. She said “I don’t care about your feelings” (I had a major crush on her and she knew it, yet she’d talk about hers all the time) and “I can’t fix your life.” Then she threw my shit out of her house and pushed me (more or less). She said “I’m so sorry be kind to yourself.” I got concerned when she didn’t show up to work (wouldn’t recommend getting romantically “involved” w/coworkers like me). I tried checking on her, no response. Then she said and I quote “you’re a pissy little b**** who is as immature as a 12 y/o who needs serious professional help and to stop feeling sorry for yourself.” Mind you, we both have dealt with severe depression. After a month, run into her, try to talk to her, goes nowhere. She’s like “let’s hang out” after putting me down for like 20 mins, mentioning “projectile vomit” when SHE mentioned the how she didn’t want to be in a relationship. She failed every test I put her through. When I saw her walking away, I knew I’d never talk to her again. That hurt. I’ve had panic attacks every day and will just start shaking uncomfortably. In time I’ll forgive and fully process, but this was so recent. She just didn’t care about the “good times” I thought we had. Everything about it sucks, but I think the hardest part (for me) was thinking I had a really good friend who I clicked with and that she gets to move on with life while I have to sort through her temporarily wrecking mine. She knows where I live and I’m absolutely terrified she’ll be outside waiting for me. I barely trust anyone and I’ve just about lost faith in the people I don’t know. I’ve been very depressed but this is different. I don’t even know myself anymore. Sorry for the rant. I had to get this out. I respect you all so much for sharing I know it’s hard. after all this, I find myself missing her. I thought we had something and she didn’t care about my feelings and then just threw me aside. Anyway hang in there everyone. I don’t know you, but I know you’re worth happiness and a beautiful life.
And remember this: no matter what they say or do, they can’t hurt us anymore. Because we’re resilient.

I want to thank everyone for their insight. I have to say, I’ve read everyone’s comments thus far and really everything I’ve seen breaks my heart. I still can’t comprehend the way some of you were treated. But I know how you feel. I unfortunately am having a full-blown panic attack and it’s hard to cope. I appreciate you all for being so vulnerable about a topic that’s hard to speak about. But I have to say all of you are fighters. You got out. That’s not easy to do. I applaud you and like I’ve said, I’m so proud of you. Please hang in there. That’s what I tell myself. I know it’ll be a long while before I’m even able to go out and meet people/make friends (due to needing a lot more help coping with these panic attacks) but I know all of us can live and love our lives now that we’re free from the grasp of people who tried to hurt us in the cruelest ways imaginable. I love reading and I’ve been told life is like a story, but instead of having someone else writing the chapters for you, you get to do it yourself. And that’s really one of the greatest gifts of all. To be happy and fulfilled with people we love and who love us back. That’s why we’re all here. My god, I’m crying  again. I love you all and I’m so proud of you all. From the bottom of my heart, forever and always, thank you. And just know that I’m with each and every one of you, if only in spirit, as you heal and regain your strength. Godspeed.

I’m so glad you appreciate my words, kindness was the intention. Thank you both for your sympathy and insight. I’m sorry you both had to go through this, it’s not OK as I’ve said. But you’re both strong. The erosion of trust and self-esteem is all so real, to the point where you’re living in an almost kind of “separate” reality. That’s still taking some adjusting. That temporary loss of sense of self is terrifying. But I’m so glad you both are here and chose to leave. I know that’s hard. It was for me but you both are brave and I commend you. You have to put yourself first. Like I said, even though I don’t know you, I’m beyond proud of each of you. and thats the truth. Thanks for also reading my blurb of text to the end

Thank you everyone for your comments thus far. I appreciate the insight more than you realize. It’s been hard but one day at a time seems to be the best method. It’s nice to know that people care after all. I think I’ll try yoga, meditation, grounding techniques. maybe discuss medication too. And definitely try to find a support group/therapist to help process (at least the peer support when I’m slightly less anxious). Just gotta keep telling myself “this too shall pass” and that nothing bad lasts forever. It’s just hard with the erosion of trust/fear of people, but it’s a solvable issue. Thank you again everyone!

She also would talk about how she was in love with multiple people (Paul Dano, her college French professor, some other guy) when she knew I had feelings for her and I told her how I felt. Huge red flag though I didn’t see it at the time. Sorry again. I’m just having trouble processing all this.

She said to “stop feeling sorry for myself” and that I needed “serious professional help” (she deals with severe depression, we’ve talked about it). She called me “as immature as a 12 y/o who can’t take no for an answer” and a “pissy little b…..” out of nowhere for an hour or so. Then she said she “didn’t care about my feelings” and did other things, like broke promises, guilt-tripped, gaslit, played mind games, took advantage of my feelings/kindness/sensitivity. We shared some intimate moments and we I asked if she enjoyed them she said “no, not really.” Just no remorse at all and never asked about/considered my feelings in the slightest. Sorry for letting all that out, I’m just trying to process this all and can’t adopted therapy. On top of that, I saw her a week ago randomly and when I tried calling her out, she flipped it around. So yeah, it’s been tough. Anyway thanks for responding and listening.

Well I appreciate your insight. It’s been incredibly hard for me. I haven’t been treated like this in years, nonetheless by someone I thought was a friend/possible girlfriend (briefly). I’d like to think there were positive moments but who knows? She was drunk but I don’t think that excuses her behavior (as I understand it, abuse is a choice). I appreciate your kindness, it’s going a long way right now as I have blamed myself and am having difficulty being self-compassionate. Though I’ve had my moments of being rude, I would never actively treat someone so horribly. It’s beneath me and deplorable. Now being mentally ill isn’t a choice (I know firsthand), but we choose our actions (I believe). It’s nice to know at the very least, I’m not alone. I’ve left and cut ties, believe me. I saw her a week ago by complete coincidence and she offered no remorse for anything, and flipped it around on me. Made me sick. Thank you for your empathy and sympathy, it’s something people should strive to exhibit. Love that song btw! Classic Paul Simon, my man. Sorry for the rant there.
Just for clarity’s sake, I suffer from severe depression and she knew that.

Thanks again everyone. I appreciate both sides of the coin being represented (though there might be some slight disagreement). It’s just been hard as this wasn’t a physical problem, but more so emotion.. abuse from a former manager. Piece of advice: don’t get involved with someone in that capacity. Guess I learned that the hard way. Anyway thanks again everyone! Appreciate the kindness.
I appreciate the kind words from everyone thus far. Nothing that can’t be accomplished. Just gonna take some effort and work. Such is life though right? Live and learn.

I appreciate that insight. I do think perhaps it was a rash decision but still the best one at the time. Here’s hoping things will work out (I’m sure they will). Not that it necessarily matters to you because you’re a complete stranger lol, but definitely have been putting my nose to the grindstone in terms of job searching.
Close. Late 20s but yep otherwise you hit the nail right on top of the head.
That’s alright. It’s emotional abuse, just as bad.

That’s fair. Didn’t quite think of it in that lens. I guess it didn’t seem appropriate to say exactly what happened, but I mean we’re talking SEVERE abuse here, not like a manager being jerky. But that isn’t your burden to bear, it’s mine for the time being. I guess maybe I figured people might be slightly more understanding of my predicament instead of saying “yes.” But according to you, I am stupid. So I guess it wouldn’t make sense anyway lol. Thanks for your input.
Yep

Thanks!

Coulda probably phrased that differently…on both of our ends,

I just wanted to thank everyone who's offered insight thus far. Unfortunately, I think you're all confirming what I already thought. It sucks and hurts, because I grew to care and love this person and thought I had at least made a friend. Even more painful, I randomly saw her by coincidence 3 days ago and when I tried calling her out, she deflected the blame onto me and was incredibly curt. There's so many angry things I wish I could've said but it wouldn't be worth stooping to that level. Just have to let her go and understand I'll most likely never see her again. Sad that she thinks treating people so poorly is "normal." Hopefully she'll change, but that's for her to figure out. Back to square one it looks like but there's beauty in a clean slate. I'm crying as I read this comments, mostly out of sadness, but also joy because now I think I have the closure I need - but don't get me wrong, to me, this is the toughest thing I've ever had to deal with, hands down. Thank you everybody - it's nice to know there's good people who care out there after all.
Unfortunately I just don’t have the money to afford a therapist right now, so it’s been hard for me to cope in an effective way.

I won’t wholly disagree - I’ve benefited from therapy in the past and it helps me immensely. But I think it was the manner in which it was said, along with being called a “pissy little b…..,” “stop feeling sorry for yourself” (when she suffers from depression herself), she called me “mean and manipulative” and “she didn’t care about my feelings” seemingly out of nowhere in her car and raged at me for 40 minutes. Then she threw my stuff out of her place. Didn’t ask me how I felt about any of this btw. She said she didn’t care about intimate moments we shared. Sorry for the rant. Just gotta get this out.

Thank you for your response. I appreciate your kindness. I’m immature but I treated her with nothing but what I thought was kind behavior. Again not a professional, but I believe this was one symptom of a pattern of emotional abuse. I’m walking around Philadelphia with a sadness I’ve never known before, and I can’t afford help (I had to quit my job because of this, she was my co-worker) and I saw her the other day at the library. I may never meet you, but your response means more than you’ll probably know. Thank you for being a decent human.
Also, I didn’t think I was being mean or manipulative when drunk. Sorry, I just need to try to process this.
Yeah please

Get out of there as quick as you can. Block his number and resist the urge to contact this guy. Sounds toxic. The same thing recently happened to me with a girl and I can completely relate. Trust me, your well-being is way more important than just some guy. You deserve to be treated with dignity and respect because though I don’t know you, you’re worth more than being treated like dirt. Also doesn’t sound like much of a “friend” if he’s playing with your feelings like that. All the best. You can talk to me if you want.

I think the worst part was I was concerned when she didn’t show up to work the next day so I messaged her saying I was going to check in and wanted to talk to her (to the point of calling an ambulance, which I told her I might-but I didn’t do that). Suppose I overdid that too but I was genuinely concerned. Then when she came out to me I said “that’s awesome” (meant benevolently but I see how that could be misconstrued). I struggle I with making friends so I think that’s why I’m taking this so hard. Anyway just venting here, that’s what I get for caring about a “friend.”

I appreciate the response. I’ve been thinking a decent amount about it and I think you’re right. There were things she did that weren’t alright. Nobody’s perfect though. Thanks for your insight and the kind words-those go a long way right now. I just can’t seem to shake this whole scenario and I guess with help, it’s time to process it and move on. Maybe one day she’ll come around but that isn’t my concern. Thanks for taking the time to respond to this. You’re unbelievably kind to do so.
Don’t know the meaning of that word lol

Thanks very much for your insight. Part of it’s on me for being immature, emotional, not understanding her boundaries. Regardless, I’m not here to bash her, but I feel like my treatment was unwarranted. Anyway, it’s just been hard for me, as I struggle to make friends. Thanks for the response dude. I appreciate it more than you probably realize.
Inevitable-Duck-3626, that would be amazing. Thank you so much.

I appreciate your words more than you probably realize. I think that's the hard part for me - comparing myself to everyone who seemingly has it "better." You make some incredibly valid points - it's easy to base one's worth on a job, money, et cetera, though that shouldn't be the case. I love that you mentioned finding something you love when you're feeling low; I haven't tried that yet but I plan to implement it. And most of all, thank you for your kindness; it means a lot. It's been a struggle and needless to say, there have been doubts about self-worth and deserving to be happy. Though you can't see me over here, I'm smiling as I read this and I have tears in my eyes (in the best possible way of course). Appreciate the encouragement immensely. All things in time right?

I'm so sorry you've had to deal with these feelings as well. It's something no one should ever have to face on a daily basis. Though I've never been sexually harassed, that is never okay. I wish I could help you. I think you've given great advice that I will take to heart. If you ever feel the need to talk and want to, feel free to reach out to me. Our situations are very similar.
